solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support, then scold, inferior

parts.note: to second a motion or a person is to back it
to rate someone is an old sense meaning to berate them

explanation.surface: Someone backs a colleague, then tells them off for poor work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' is just the order of the two pieces; RATE in the sense of scold is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-rate is of mediocre quality, a common synonym for inferior.

clue.text: Problem in adding ring for foreign form of fighting

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A puzzle about adding a ring to a type of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as a boxing ring; it only gives the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling, a combat sport from abroad.

clue.text: In county, foolishly plays number of West Indians

indicators.note: In tells us the jumbled letters go inside the county's abbreviation
foolishly says the letters of plays are thrown around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of Caribbean people playing the fool somewhere in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song, not a count; the definition is a song of the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a style of song from Trinidad and the Caribbean, so one is a musical piece of that region.

clue.text: Preserving organisation in part of Bible? Initially it could be

definitions.text: Preserving organisation in part of Bible? Initially it could be

parts.note: the body that conserves historic houses and land in Britain

parts.words: in part of Bible? Initially it could be
parts.note: its initials match the abbreviation for the New Testament, a part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a conservation charity could be found in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust conserves historic buildings and countryside in England, Wales and Northern Ireland; its initials NT also stand for New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Trust is the British charity devoted to preserving heritage properties and landscapes.

clue.text: Reach logical conclusions about a child

parts.note: re means concerning
taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Drawing deductions regarding a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to think through a matter and arrive at a judgement by logic.

clue.text: Doing exercises in minimal temperature, then showering

parts.note: the minimal part of temperature is its first letter, T
showering, like rain, gives raining

explanation.surface: Working out in freezing weather in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is practising or working out to build fitness or skill.

clue.text: Covering a sound sleeper?

parts.note: taken as written
the idiom 'sleep like a top' makes a spinning top the classic sound sleeper

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a duvet or blanket for someone who sleeps deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinning top that turns so steadily it seems motionless is said to sleep, hence 'sleep like a top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, so a thing atop another is lying over or covering it.

clue.text: Wear the writer out, crossing river in ancient vessel

indicators.note: crossing means the word for wearing out spans the river

parts.note: to wear someone out is to tire them
the setter refers to themself, giving me

explanation.surface: A rower is exhausted after crossing a river in an old boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear ... out' together mean tire; 'out' rounds off that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient Greek or Roman war galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Summon artist producing exciting work

parts.note: to page someone is to call them, over a tannoy or pager
J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: Calling in a painter to create a thrilling piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so gripping the reader cannot stop reading.

clue.text: Armed civilians prepare to fire back across one line with it

indicators.note: across says the reversed word spans the following pieces, enclosing them
back says the word for preparing to fire is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: before shooting you take aim
one as the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteer fighters ready their weapons and shoot back along a defensive line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare to fire' looks like part of the surface story, but it is the clued word to be turned around and opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a military force raised from ordinary citizens rather than professional soldiers.

clue.text: Declaring a short volume outstanding

parts.note: taken as written
V is the short form, or abbreviation, of volume
a debt that is outstanding is still owing

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a brief book is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the book, but it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly, so avowing is a synonym of declaring.

clue.text: Until governed in reformed way, too permissive

indicators.note: reformed means the letters are formed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lax until they were ruled in a reformed fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An overindulgent parent or ruler is excessively lenient, allowing too much.

clue.text: Declaration you or I, say, stick at the end

indicators.note: at the end places the word for stick last in the answer

parts.note: you and I are both examples of a pronoun, as 'say' signals
to cement is to stick things together

explanation.surface: Someone tacks a personal statement onto the end of an announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal or authoritative statement, a synonym of declaration.

clue.text: Equally, it's central for school-leaver

parts.note: the answer means shared in equal halves
the two middle letters of the word school-leaver are LL, each L being fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A remark on what matters most for a young person leaving school.
explanation.walkthrough: SCHOOL-LEAVER has twelve letters and its middle pair is LL; L is 50 in Roman numerals, so the centre reads fifty, fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty-fifty means divided in equal halves, so it serves as the adverb equally.

clue.text: I accordingly must join legal group on which pressure is constant

parts.note: taken as written
so, meaning therefore
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Reads like someone obliged to join the legal profession under constant pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bar is the collective name for barristers, the courtroom lawyers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Skilfully arrange language that's brief, stylish, and always poetic

parts.note: Eng is the short form of English
in, as in fashionable
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Advice on arranging words: keep them brief, stylish and poetic.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER drops its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a result is to contrive or bring it about by clever planning.

clue.text: In taking over, normal person put in charge

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new leader takes over in an ordinary handover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking over' and 'put in charge' make it look like a definition-heavy clue, but the answer is spelt out in the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is someone appointed to run a state, colony, prison or institution.

clue.text: Act of pulling drunk into cart

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reeling about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hauling an intoxicated man up into a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the action of drawing or hauling a load along a surface.

clue.text: Display armour in overseas post?

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly
mail is armour of linked rings

explanation.surface: Showing off a suit of armour at a foreign posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a military posting abroad, but it is letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is letters and parcels carried by aircraft, typically sent abroad.

clue.text: It's all right to scoff as I bleed terribly

indicators.note: terribly says the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wounded person tells someone mocking them it's fine to jeer while they bleed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mocking, but here it means to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is fit to be eaten, and scoff is informal for eat.

clue.text: What non-profit organisations do a good deal

definitions.meaning: a purchase at a low price

explanation.surface: Charities strike a favourable agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words: to bar gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something bought cheaply, a good deal for the buyer.

clue.text: Fit in part of label on garment

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a section of the following words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Checking whether clothing fits by its label.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to be accepted and at home in a place or group.

clue.text: Since bank worker is hiding strain, who knows what is going to happen?

definitions.text: who knows what is going to happen?

indicators.note: is hiding means the first pieces conceal the melody between them

parts.note: for, as in 'for he was tired'
a teller handles customers at a bank counter
a strain is a melody, a tune

explanation.surface: A bank clerk concealing stress wonders what the future holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like stress, but it is a musical strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller claims to predict future events, which the question-as-definition describes.

clue.text: Gave rise to bishop and cardinal, say

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
cardinal is a shade of red, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: A bishop and a cardinal produced something between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' reads as a churchman beside the bishop; here it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to produce or engender, so bred means caused or produced.

clue.text: Add weight, about pound — or remove bulge?

indicators.note: about tells us the word for adding weight goes around the pound

parts.note: to fatten is to make heavier
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A dieter weighing whether to gain a pound or lose the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten something is to make it level, removing any bump or swelling.

clue.text: Get nothing to write song for this kind of concert

parts.note: O looks like zero
to pen is to write
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A musician has nothing and must compose a song for a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air concert is held outdoors rather than in a hall.

clue.text: Thief might gain entrance after picking this university

definitions.text: Thief might gain entrance after picking this
definitions.meaning: a common brand of cylinder lock, which a burglar might pick
... University in Connecticut, one of the Ivy League

explanation.surface: Suggests a burglar choosing which university to break into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking' looks like choosing, but it means opening a lock without its key.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by the lock maker and the American Ivy League university.

clue.text: Cheered up after book's corrected

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
to righten is to set right, so rightened means corrected

explanation.surface: Someone is happier once their book has been put right.
explanation.walkthrough: RIGHTEN is a rare but dictionary verb meaning to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To brighten up is to become more cheerful, a synonym of cheering up.
